title: Irregular sinkhole bowl, clipped fissures and supplied quake audio
context: The owner found the initial circular cutout unsatisfying and requested a sloping descent toward blackness that reads as climbable, cracks outside the hole and the supplied quake/break MP3.
outcome: The floor cut, fissure clip and bowl share one irregular radius contract. A textured bowl with a gentler approach and steeper side walls fades into a small irregular black throat; rim rubble breaks the edge. Opening slabs subside, dust settles and debris collides with the actual slope rather than flat y=0. The unmodified owner-provided 6.984-second clip is pinned locally and played through the shared mixer at pre-roll start; mute, reset, genre exit and disposal stop it. This remains a planar lab effect, with no enemy navigation or gameplay spawn replacement.
alternatives: The old circular void and plate left floating-looking fissures and no readable route into the ground.
Persistent reference dust obscured the bowl; post-opening emission now decays.
Use one CPU/GLSL boundary contract rather than separate approximate circles for cracks, floor and slope.
evidence: npm test: 76 programs passed, including irregularity, monotonic slope and approach-angle tests.
npm run check and npm run build passed; imported adaptations and supplied audio hashes verified.
node scripts/browser-test.mjs --sinkhole passed texture/shader load, active quake voice, settled bowl, reset/reopen, genre return and disposal.
docs/SINKHOLE.md records ownership, supplied audio and the future navigation/sphere boundary.
